title: What the 2025 INCB precursor report says about China-linked incidents—and what it does not prove
dek: Nine reported incidents, nearly five tonnes, and one crucial missing join: the official record identifies an origin, but it does not establish a causal chain to US deaths or measure lawful industrial trade.

sections.heading: What the INCB report actually says

sentences.text: INCB reported that, during the first ten months of 2025, 9 incidents involving nearly 5 tonnes of two related methamphetamine pre-precursors were communicated through PICS.

citationLocators.locator: paragraph 94; PDF page 44; printed page 26

sentences.text: The report said those substances were mislabelled, reportedly originated in China and were destined for countries in the European Union.

citationLocators.locator: paragraph 94; PDF page 44; printed page 26

sentences.text: That figure is a less-than multi-incident aggregate, not an exact 5,000 kg shipment, and NarcoScope does not add it to other qualified quantities.

citationLocators.locator: paragraph 94; PDF page 44; printed page 26

sentences.text: For Operation Pseudonym, INCB said four participating countries reported 168 seizures, most in Australia and New Zealand, and reported China and India as origins in those two countries.

citationLocators.locator: paragraph 46; PDF page 31; printed page 13

sentences.text: The public report does not allocate those seizures or their mass by origin-and-destination pair; Australia’s and New Zealand’s annual totals are separate aggregates and are excluded here.

sentences.text: Across every retained December checkpoint, CDC’s provisional US count involving synthetic opioids excluding methadone rose from 9,610 in 2015 to a peak of 74,829 in 2022, then fell 48.6% to 38,458 in 2025.

sections.heading: The evidence gap is the finding

sentences.text: The official record supports one attributed finding: INCB reported a China-origin aggregate of nearly five tonnes across nine incidents bound for European Union countries.

citationLocators.locator: paragraph 94; PDF page 44; printed page 26

sentences.text: It supports zero independently corroborated event claims because no second admitted source confirms the same incident set at compatible grain.

sources.publisher: General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China
sources.title: China Customs Statistics
sources.accessNote: Public web tables and releases; the English interactive-table surface is not a stable bulk API.
sources.licensingNote: Official statistics are publicly viewable, but NarcoScope has not identified terms authorizing bulk redistribution; link and cite unless permission is confirmed.

sources.title: UN Comtrade Database and API
sources.accessNote: A keyless preview API is public and limited; free registered API access has quotas; bulk access and some redistribution require a subscription or licence.
sources.licensingNote: Use is governed by the UN Comtrade usage agreement; redistribution of large original extracts can require a separate licence, while transformed data is treated differently.

sources.title: Precursors Report 2025
sources.accessNote: Public annual PDF; selected aggregates retain printed page and paragraph locators, quantity relations and extraction derivations.
sources.licensingNote: Public UN publication; NarcoScope republishes a small attributed factual extract, not the report text.

sources.title: Precursors Incident Communication System (PICS)
sources.accessNote: Secure system for registered government regulatory, customs, drug-control and law-enforcement users.
sources.licensingNote: Operational records are not a public dataset and are not licensed for NarcoScope redistribution.

sources.title: Pre-Export Notification Online (PEN Online)
sources.accessNote: Secure pre-export-notification system for registered competent national authorities.
sources.licensingNote: Notification records are not a public dataset and are not licensed for NarcoScope redistribution.
